key_insight: In a double-blind clinical study, blood metabolic profiles combined with AI could help distinguish children with ASD from those with other developmental delays.
clinical_relevance: If validated in larger cohorts, this approach could support earlier, more objective ASD diagnostic evaluation in developmental pediatric settings.
method: 140 children aged 18–60 months from diagnostic waitlists at two pediatric clinics
Blood metabolic profiles were collected alongside gold-standard assessments (ADOS, MSEL, VABS) and full clinical review
DSM-5-based clinical diagnosis was used as the reference standard for ASD vs non-ASD delay
evidence_signal: Using metabolite data, AI-based classifiers achieved over 80% accuracy for predicting whether a sample came from a child with ASD.
watch_item: The study needs replication in larger, more diverse samples, especially with more non-ASD developmental delay cases, before clinical implementation.
paper_title: Translational Study of using FOCM/TS Metabolites for Supporting Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis
